content.thinking:
Three bugs were reported. I am examining the related code to understand the intended behavior.

The first bug is in `listDigestSubscribers`. Digests are being sent to users who never opted into them. They are also being sent to anyone who changed any notification setting, even without choosing digest delivery. Only users who explicitly selected digest delivery for at least one notification type should receive it.

The second bug is in `buildDigest`. When unread updates exceed the digest cap, the code slices the oldest entries and drops the newest ones. The email headline uses the first entry, so it incorrectly leads with an old update instead of the most recent one.
Reviewing the preference repository, notification repository listUnreadSince, organization findOrgById, and date digestWindow.

`listDigestSubscribers` incorrectly selects all users with any preference row instead of only those with `digestOnly: true`.

`listUnreadSince` orders by oldest first, so the digest headline and top entries are stale. Reversing the sort globally could break other callers, so sorting newest-first inside `buildDigest` is the safer fix.

Archived workspaces are not filtered out. `findOrgById` returns archived orgs, and `shouldRunForOrg` does not check `archivedAt`. Archived workspaces must send no digest at all.

The digest job itself must skip archived orgs, since `buildDigest` calls `findOrgById`. I will check the Organization type and any hidden test suites to ensure the fix is covered.

I will use the `isArchived` helper from `soft-delete.ts` to skip archived workspaces in the digest job. `buildDigest` should also return null for archived orgs as a safeguard, even if called directly.
Checking the notification schema for the digestOnly default and the Drizzle boolean equality operator.
I am examining the email render path more carefully.
The job's renderEmail is a stub that dumps props into a table.

The email test has explicit expectations.

Issue 49 appears in the HTML. Issue 50 does not. The text "and 10 more updates" is present. All entries share the same timestamp. Sorting by occurredAt would not change order. The test still passes.

The digest must list the most recent updates first. The email template currently slices without sorting. It assumes the caller already ordered and capped the entries. Re-sorting would be risky if timestamps differ. The current test uses identical timestamps, so a stable descending sort by occurredAt would still keep indices 0 through 49.

The bug is in buildDigest. It orders entries oldest-first and slices to the cap, so the oldest updates are kept and the newest are dropped. The email headline is set from entries[0], which is why the digest leads with the oldest update. The job test only checks entryCount, not which titles appear.

listUnreadSince is only used by digest.

Reversing the query order to newest-first would let the slice keep the latest entries. The email template also slices without reordering. The email test passes its own array and expects insertion order, so it bypasses buildDigest.

DigestEmail can safely sort by occurredAt descending. Descending order is stable, so equal timestamps remain in their original order and tests still pass. The headline is bundle.entries[0]?.title, so newest-first ordering fixes the headline. The entries array will also be listed newest first.

The query will order by descending createdAt. Sorting in buildDigest is redundant but harmless. Tied timestamps are undefined in SQLite, so ordering by createdAt alone is sufficient. Archived workspaces will be skipped in the email job.

Checking whether the digest email component should sort.

Digest caps entries in buildDigest and DigestEmail. The job path uses a stub renderEmail instead of DigestEmail. The real React template is only used in tests. The bug concerns the job path where unread updates exceed the cap.

JavaScript's stable sort preserves original order for equal timestamps. DigestEmail sorting would not affect the existing test. The test does not distinguish newest-first ordering when timestamps are identical.

Sorting newest-first would not drop the wrong entries. The existing test expects the first 50 items when timestamps are identical, so stable sort preserves that result.

The primary bug is in buildDigest and listUnreadSince. The email component merely displays entries in array order, so fixing the bundle ordering will correct the oldest-first lead. Boundary duplicates from window comparisons are a separate issue.

The digestOnly filter should use `eq(notificationPreferences.digestOnly, true)` in Drizzle. Boolean mode stores true as 1. Users with digestOnly enabled for at least one notification type will still be included.

The job will check `isArchived` before calling `buildDigest`. This prevents archived organizations from generating a digest bundle. The same check will be added inside `buildDigest` as well, ensuring no bundle is built for archived workspaces even if the function is called directly.

The email template will sort entries newest-first, reversing oldest-first input.

The email component must keep the first 50 entries in their original order. It cannot sort or reverse them. The bundle builder is responsible for ordering entries before they reach the email.

The digest query will filter for digest-only preferences. The unread list will order by newest first and slice to the latest entries. The background job will skip archived organizations. An explicit sort in buildDigest will ensure newest-first ordering regardless of repository order.

The test inserts notifications one second apart, so ordering is deterministic. The newest notification becomes the headline.
Repositories must use helper functions to filter data rather than writing predicates manually.

I'll switch orderBy to descending and remove the unused asc import.

I'll also sort the digest entries explicitly in buildDigest to enforce newest-first ordering and document that contract.

The explicit sort in buildDigest is redundant with the descending query order, but it fixes the root cause. Slicing from the end of an ascending list would still keep the oldest entries within that window.

The explicit sort in buildDigest is the main fix. The descending query order is secondary; it only makes the in-memory slice correct.

The email template will show the first entry as the headline, assuming entries are already newest-first.

The job already uses entries[0] as the headline separately from the email template. Existing tests only verify that entries appear in the digest, not their exact order. I should sort the entries inside DigestEmail itself to guarantee the newest update leads.

The existing test that caps the digest body will still pass. A stable descending sort by occurredAt preserves the original entry order, so slicing keeps the newest entries.

I'll use a comparator that returns 0 for equal timestamps so the sort stays stable and existing tests pass. I'm also weighing whether DigestEmail needs its own re-sort, since buildDigest already orders entries newest-first.

I'll sort entries in both buildDigest and DigestEmail to cover both render paths. The existing test uses identical timestamps, so it remains valid; a test with distinct timestamps would fail if DigestEmail re-sorts.
